comparison: Both evaluations agree that AF2 fails to generate appropriate holo structures for type II inhibitor binding. OpenEval focuses on C1, C11, C12, C38, C40 while peer review includes C39 as well. Both cite quantitative RMSD data and established knowledge about AF2's limitations with metastable conformations.

Perfect claim overlap (C13-C21). Both evaluations support the ensemble generation and structural analysis findings. OpenEval provides detailed quantitative assessment of DDR1 vs Abl1 results and IFD-trim protocol. Peer review implicitly accepts these findings while focusing on overall workflow limitations.

Perfect claim overlap (C22-C27). Both evaluations support the SPIB-based enrichment approach with quantitative PMF values. OpenEval emphasizes orthogonal validation through DiffDock and consistency between umbrella sampling and unbiased MD. Peer review explicitly endorses the RAVE-based enrichment methodology.

High claim overlap (C28-C32). Both evaluations support AF2-template success and transferability findings. OpenEval focuses on comparative failure of rMSA AF2 and AF2-cluster for Abl1, while peer review emphasizes cross-kinase transferability (DDR1 to Abl1 and Src).

Partial claim overlap (C35, C36). Both evaluations support transferability to Src kinase. OpenEval notes limited data presentation, while peer review groups this with broader comparative analyses (C33, C34) demonstrating strengths/weaknesses of different AF2-based methods.

High claim overlap (C2, C3, C37). Both evaluations strongly support the 50% enrichment achievement as the main result. OpenEval provides specific quantitative breakdown from Table 1, while peer review emphasizes all reviewers' affirmation of AF2RAVE's success and editor's endorsement.

High claim overlap (C5, C43, C45, C46). Both evaluations support the integration of physics-based methods with AF2. OpenEval emphasizes the non-Boltzmann nature of rMSA ensembles and practical necessity of RAVE. Peer review explicitly endorses combining AF2 with RAVE to address diversity and weighting limitations.

Perfect claim overlap (C4, C7-C10). Both evaluations support these established background claims about kinase biology and inhibitor classification. OpenEval notes appropriate citations and consistency with literature. Peer review accepts these as uncontroversial background facts, with Reviewer 1 explicitly acknowledging the DFG motif context.

Perfect claim overlap (C41, C42). Both evaluations support these literature-based claims about prior AF2 work. OpenEval verifies accurate representation of cited sources. Peer review accepts these as established prior work providing appropriate context for the current study.

High claim overlap (C47, C48). Disagreement on status: OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature and lack of systematic validation across multiple systems. Peer review rates SUPPORTED, viewing these forward-looking perspectives as implicitly endorsed through praise of the demonstrated integration approach and promising future directions.

Peer review groups C33, C34 with C35, C36 as comparative analyses of AF2-based methods. OpenEval addresses C33, C34 separately in R4 (with different claims) and C35, C36 in R5. Peer review takes a broader view of comparative method evaluation as a unified finding.

Minimal overlap (C44 only). OpenEval groups C44 with other forward-looking claims (C47, C48) and rates UNCERTAIN. Peer review groups C44 with methodology claims (C5, C43, C45, C46) and rates SUPPORTED, viewing it as part of the validated integration approach rather than speculation.
